anomalies.observed: R8 is valued "24k" (24 kΩ) in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its own description and MPN specify a 24 Ω 0805 part (FRC0805J240TSD, "125mW ... 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor").
anomalies.expected: A 24 Ω resistor, matching the library description and MPN, across the VOUTP/VOUTN output. A 24 kΩ value would not match the part that was sourced.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R8") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS") ... (field (name "MPN") "FRC0805J240TSD")

anomalies.impact: The value is inconsistent with the sourced part. Depending on which value is actually fitted, the output-side load or bleed behaviour differs substantially from the intended design.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three Ethernet/status LEDs D5, D8 and D22 are tied only to each other on net /NET0061. That net has no connection to +3V3 or any other supply, so the LED loop has no drive path.
anomalies.expected: The LED anode common node should be tied to a supply rail (typically +3V3), with the cathodes driven through their series resistors from the Ethernet nLED pins.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity and link indicator LEDs cannot light because no anode supply exists, so the status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U9 and U16 have both their GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) pins on the same global GND net, so the isolated side is not separated from the logic ground.
anomalies.expected: The GND2 side of an isolated CAN transceiver should be on an isolated ground, separate from the controller's GND, as the specification requires for the isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design relies on is defeated, so the CAN bus shares ground with the controller, leaving the bus exposed to ground-loop and fault-current paths.
